registered_before: any percentile rank, exceedance share, interval or null value of this study was computed or viewed. Seen before registration: SPARTACUS metadata (period, licence), one raw SPARTACUS series for a single point (request-size probe, values not analysed), cohort counts per year/process/episode.
status: EXPLORATORY: all 423 events were already used in V0.4/V0.5. Nothing in this study is a confirmation; the confirmation plan for unseen events is reports/extremwetter_v01/CONFIRMATION_PLAN.md.
question: Was precipitation before the documented event day at the event location more extreme than on comparable days without a documented event at the same location? (case-crossover, same place, different days)

cohort.rows: label == 1 (one positive per event group), date tier A (all rows of this run are tier A)
cohort.independence_unit: temporal episode: single linkage over local event days with gap <= 3 days (preslide.v04.units.temporal_episodes)
cohort.stanz_episode: the temporal episode containing local day 2016-07-25

weather.day_semantics: RR labelled day D = station-based sum 07:00 CET D -> 07:00 CET D+1 (06:00 UTC D+1), provider metadata
weather.location: event coordinate (latitude/longitude of the V0.4 positive); nearest 1 km cell returned by the API; offset must be <= 800 m (EPSG:31287)
weather.plausibility: every value used must be finite and in [0, 500] mm; otherwise the run fails (no clipping, no filling)
weather.cache: raw responses cached under data/extremwetter_v01/cache/http with URL + SHA-256 sidecar

exposure.variable: precipitation sum over k consecutive SPARTACUS days

primary.meaning: last SPARTACUS day = event day - 2, i.e. precipitation measured up to 07:00 CET of the day before the event day. Strictly before t0 for every event (t0 >= local midnight of the event day); this is the V0.4 daily admissibility rule (D+1 06:00 UTC < t0) applied with the earliest possible t0.

secondary_previous_day.meaning: includes 00:00-07:00 local of the event day; rain after the event may be included

secondary_event_day.meaning: includes the whole event day until 07:00 of the next day; contains rain after the event. Descriptive only, never evidence of a pre-event signal

placebo.meaning: 3-day window ending 60 days before the primary window end, outside every primary window; expected percentile rank 0.5 unless year-level wetness or a trend biases the reference

reference.design: time-stratified, same 1 km cell, same calendar window in other years (bidirectional)
reference.anchor_rule: for each reference year Y != event year: anchor day = (event day with year set to Y; 29 Feb -> 28 Feb) + offset, offset in [-15, +15] days (31 anchors per year). Year boundaries handled by date arithmetic (a 5 January event uses 21 Dec of Y-1 to 20 Jan of Y).
reference.reference_window: each anchor gets exactly the same window definition (length k, same last-label offset) as the event
reference.event_year_excluded: the whole event year is excluded so that no reference window shares the triggering storm or its season

documented_event_exclusion.inventory: data/raw/geosphere_natural_hazards.json (GeoSphere Naturgefahren, local snapshot), all quality levels
documented_event_exclusion.dated_records: records with Date_Anfan and Date_End_a, converted to local (Europe/Vienna) days, interval length <= 31 days; longer or missing intervals are counted and ignored (too vague to place a day)
documented_event_exclusion.rule: an anchor day r is excluded if a dated record within radius_m has a day interval intersecting [r - days, r + days]

reference.outside_series: anchors whose window reaches outside the downloaded series are dropped and counted
reference.below_minimum: the event is excluded from that analysis and counted by reason

statistics.percentile_rank: PR = (#reference < x + 0.5 * #reference == x) / #reference (mid-rank, ties split). Smallest value -> 0 (if strictly smallest), largest -> 1 (if strictly largest). Exchangeable case => E[PR] = 0.5.
statistics.exceedance: x > Q_p of the event's own reference windows (numpy quantile, linear), p in [0.95, 0.99]; null expectation per event q_i = share of its reference windows > Q_p (about 1 - p)
statistics.rate_ratio: case-crossover odds ratio for 'window above Q_p': [s / (1 - s)] / [q / (1 - q)] with s = weighted exceedance share of events and q = weighted null expectation. Interpreted as how many times more documented events followed such windows than other days; subject to reporting bias

weighting.primary: each temporal episode weight 1 (events of an episode share 1/n_e)

bootstrap.unit: temporal episode (whole episodes resampled with replacement)

null.method: pseudo-case Monte Carlo: for each episode one common (reference year, offset) cell is drawn uniformly from the cells valid for all its events; that reference window replaces each event's case window and is ranked against the remaining (leave-one-out) reference windows of the same event. Preserves episode dependence and the spatial correlation within a storm.
null.p_value: one-sided, H1 = more extreme (larger) than reference: (1 + #null >= observed) / (1 + draws)

statistics.effective_sample_size: number of temporal episodes in the analysed set, reported next to every number

hypotheses.primary: episode-weighted mean PR of the 3-day primary window (end offset -2, reference 1991-2025) > 0.5
hypotheses.claim_rule: an increase is described (still exploratory) only if the one-sided null p < 0.05 AND the 95 % episode-bootstrap interval excludes 0.5
secondary_registered: mean PR for windows 1, 7, 14, 30 days (Holm correction over the 5 primary-end windows reported)
exceedance shares above Q95 and Q99 and their rate ratios for all 5 windows
hypotheses.multiplicity: every cell of the comparison table below is computed and reported; no cell is dropped after viewing

for_every_window: primary (episodes weighted, all events, reference 1991-2025, end -2)
plus: placebo 3-day window ending at offset -62 (primary settings)
comparisons.count: 10 settings x 5 windows + 1 placebo = 51 rows, each with mean PR, exceedance Q95/Q99 shares, rate ratios, bootstrap intervals, null p and effective sample size

reporting_bias: documented events are more completely recorded after large storms (field campaigns, media attention); this inflates the association between extreme rain and documented events. Discussed in the report; not corrected.

outputs.report: reports/extremwetter_v01/ (summary.md German, figures, comparisons.json aggregate only)
